newsitem.title: POLAND: Cieszyn up, Wroclaw down after merger news.
newsitem.headline: Cieszyn up, Wroclaw down after merger news.

text.p: Polish paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn surged 9.5 percent to 18.4 zlotys and Polifarb Wroclaw fell 7.9 percent to 15.1 zlotys after the firms' shareholders agreed on a merger earlier this week.

Wroclaw shareholders on Tuesday approved the merger planned for mid-year while on Monday Cieszyn shareholders approved a version of the merger that would give them 53.5 percent rather than a previously agreed 50 percent of the new firm.
Wroclaw officials have said a mutual shareholder, BIG might dispute Cieszyn's action in court but that the merger was still likely to go through as a delay would cost both firms.
"That (Wednesday's price moves) was a direct result of the shareholders' decisions," one trader said, alluding to the prospect that Cieszyn shareholders would get 53.5 percent.
Other traders said that Wednesday's divergent price moves were not likely to continue as Cieszyn's potential dominance in the new firm would only be slight.
